title: Algebraically closed extension for proper curves
statement:
Let $k\subseteq k'$ be an extension of algebraically closed fields [def-weil-algebraic-closure], and let $\iota:\operatorname{Spec}k'\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ be the induced morphism of spectra [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Let $C$ be a scheme over $k$ [def-weil-scheme-over-base] whose structure morphism $f:C\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is proper [def-weil-proper-morphism] and whose underlying topological space has Krull dimension $\dim C\le1$ [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension] (the empty scheme is allowed). Let $C_{k'}=C\times_{\operatorname{Spec}k}\operatorname{Spec}k'$ be the base change of $C$ along $\iota$ [def-pc-base-change], with projection $\pi:C_{k'}\to C$. Let $F$ be a torsion abelian sheaf on the small etale site $C_{\Et}$ [def-weil-pbc-torsion-etale-sheaf], and write $F|_{C_{k'}}=\pi^{-1}F$ for its inverse image [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image]. Then for every $q\ge0$ the pullback map along $\pi$ [def-weil-pbc-cohomology-pullback]

$$
 \pi^*:H^q(C_{\Et},F)\longrightarrow H^q((C_{k'})_{\Et},\pi^{-1}F)
$$

between the etale cohomology groups [def-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology] is an isomorphism. (This is item (7) of Stacks Theorem 03SC.)

proof.text: Translation into the curve assertions. A proper morphism is separated and of finite type, so $C$ is a separated $k$-scheme of finite type with $\dim C\le1$. The sheaf $F$ is torsion in the sense of [def-weil-pbc-torsion-etale-sheaf] (the map $\varinjlim_nF[n]\to F$ is an isomorphism); by [lem-weil-pbc-torsion-sheaf-characterizations] ((1)$\Leftrightarrow$(2)) this is equivalent to every local section being locally killed by a positive integer, which is the torsion condition of [def-weil-pbc-curve-setting]. Hence $(C,F)$ is a curve coefficient pair over the algebraically closed field $k$. The map $\rho^q_{k'/k}(C,F)$ of [def-weil-pbc-extension-pullback] is the pullback map in degree $q$ along the projection $\pi_{k'}=\pi:C_{k'}=C\times_kk'\to C$ with $F_{k'}=\pi^{-1}F$, i.e. the map $\pi^*$ of [def-weil-pbc-cohomology-pullback]. So the claim is exactly assertion $\mathcal C_7(C,F)$ of [def-weil-pbc-C7] for the extension $k'/k$, i.e. the seventh conjunct of $\mathcal C(C,F)$ in [def-weil-pbc-eight-curve-assertions]. Throughout, as in Stacks, for a curve coefficient pair $(X,G)$ over $k$ 'the assertions $\mathcal C(X,G)$ hold' means that those of the eight implications whose hypotheses (affine, proper, constructible, prime to $p$, $p$-primary) are met are true; and $\mathcal C(X,G)$ depends only on the isomorphism class of $G$.

source.place: Section 03SB, Situation 0A52 and the list of statements (1)-(8) after it; Theorem 03SC, item (7)

proof.text: Zero-dimensional schemes (Stacks, proof of Lemma 0A5B, first paragraph: higher etale cohomology of any sheaf on a point vanishes). Let $Z$ be a separated finite-type $k$-scheme of dimension $\le0$ and $G$ a torsion sheaf on $Z_{\Et}$. By [lem-weil-pbc-zero-dimensional-cohomology], $H^q(Z,G)=0$ for $q>0$ and $H^0(Z,G)=\prod_{z\in|Z|}G_{\bar z}$, a finite product; this gives (C1), (C2), (C3) (all groups in degrees $\ge2$ vanish), and (C4), (C5): if $G$ is constructible its restriction to each stratum of a finite partition is locally constant with finite stalks, so each $G_{\bar z}$ is finite. Every open $U\subseteq Z$ is again of dimension $\le0$, so $H^2(U,G|_U)=0$ and the restriction in (C8) is surjective. (C6) and (C7) are [lem-weil-pbc-zero-dimensional-field-extension]. Hence $\mathcal C(Z,G)$ holds [def-weil-pbc-eight-curve-assertions].

source.place: Section 03SB, proof of Lemma 0A5B (lemma-constant-smooth-statements), first paragraph

proof.text: Smooth case (Stacks Lemma 03SG, with Lemma 0A5B). Claim: if $X$ is a separated finite-type $k$-scheme with $\dim X\le1$ which is smooth over $k$ [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], $j:U\hookrightarrow X$ is an open immersion and $\ell$ is a prime, then $\mathcal C(X,j_!\underline{\mathbf Z/\ell})$ holds. Proof. $X$ is Noetherian, so it has finitely many connected components $X_1,\dots,X_m$, each open and closed; each $X_i$ is smooth and connected, hence normal with integral local rings, hence irreducible. If $\dim X_i=0$, then $X_i$ is etale over $k$ and connected, so $X_i\cong\operatorname{Spec}k$; if $\dim X_i=1$, $X_i$ is a smooth separated connected curve over $k$ in the sense of [def-sc-curves]. Let $\iota_i:X_i\hookrightarrow X$ be the inclusions (open and closed immersions, hence finite) and $j_i:U_i=U\cap X_i\hookrightarrow X_i$. Comparing geometric stalks (the stalk formula of [def-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero]), $j_!\underline{\mathbf Z/\ell}\cong\bigoplus_i\iota_{i,*}j_{i,!}\underline{\mathbf Z/\ell}$. A finite direct sum is an iterated extension by the split sequences $0\to A\to A\oplus B\to B\to0$, so by [lemma-weil-pbc-eight-curve-devissage] it suffices to prove $\mathcal C(X,\iota_{i,*}j_{i,!}\underline{\mathbf Z/\ell})$ for each $i$, and by [lem-weil-pbc-curve-assertions-finite-pushforward] (for the finite $\iota_i$) it suffices to prove $\mathcal C(X_i,j_{i,!}\underline{\mathbf Z/\ell})$. If $X_i$ is a point this is step 2. If $X_i$ is a curve and $U_i=\emptyset$ the sheaf is $0$, all its cohomology groups and pullback maps are zero, and every assertion holds trivially. Otherwise $U_i$ is a nonempty open of the irreducible $X_i$, hence dense. By [thm-sc-main] the constant sheaf $\mathbf F_\ell=\underline{\mathbf Z/\ell}$ [def-sc-constant-sheaves] satisfies $\mathcal C(X_i,\mathbf F_\ell)$: part (a) if $\ell\neq\operatorname{char}k$ ((C3) is then vacuous: $\mathbf F_\ell$ is nonzero and not $p$-primary), part (b) if $\ell=\operatorname{char}k=p$ ((C4) and (C6) are then vacuous: $\mathbf F_p$ is not prime to $p$), the conditional assertions (C2), (C5), (C7) being asserted there exactly under their hypotheses. The constant sheaf is constructible (one stratum, [def-weil-pbc-constructible-torsion]), so [lem-weil-pbc-curve-assertions-dense-open] for the dense open $j_i$ gives $\mathcal C(X_i,j_{i,!}j_i^{-1}\mathbf F_\ell)=\mathcal C(X_i,j_{i,!}\mathbf F_\ell)$.

Locally constant coefficients on an irreducible open, trace reduction (Stacks Lemma 03SD, first paragraph). Let $X$ be a reduced separated finite-type $k$-scheme with $\dim X\le1$, $j:U\hookrightarrow X$ an open immersion with $U$ irreducible, $\ell$ a prime and $G$ a finite locally constant sheaf of $\mathbf F_\ell$-vector spaces on $U$; we prove $\mathcal C(X,j_!G)$ in this and the next three steps. By [lemma-weil-pbc-curve-locally-constant-reduction] there is a connected finite etale $v:V\to U$ of degree prime to $\ell$ such that $v^{-1}G$ has a finite filtration with quotients $\underline{\mathbf Z/\ell}_V$, and the unit and trace $G\xrightarrow{\eta}v_*v^{-1}G\xrightarrow{\operatorname{tr}}G$ compose to $\deg(v)\cdot\mathrm{id}_G$, an automorphism since $\ell\nmid\deg v$ and $\ell G=0$. Applying the additive functor $j_!$, the maps $a=j_!\eta:j_!G\to H:=j_!v_*v^{-1}G$ and $b=j_!\operatorname{tr}$ satisfy $b\circ a=\deg(v)\,\mathrm{id}$. Both sheaves are killed by $\ell$, so each is torsion prime to $p=\operatorname{char}k$ if $\ell\neq p$ and $p$-primary if $\ell=p$ [def-weil-pbc-primary-torsion]; and $H$ is constructible: $v^{-1}G$ is finite locally constant on the Noetherian $V$ (one stratum), $v_*v^{-1}G$ is constructible on $U$ by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-pushforward-constructible-noetherian] ($v$ is finite), and its extension by zero is constructible on $X$ (the strata of $U$ together with the closed complement $X\setminus U$, on which it is $0$) [def-weil-pbc-constructible-torsion]. By [lem-weil-pbc-curve-assertions-retract] it suffices to prove $\mathcal C(X,j_!v_*v^{-1}G)$.

proof.text: Compactifying $V$ over $X$ (Stacks Lemma 03SD, Zariski's main theorem). The composite $j\circ v:V\to X$ is quasi-finite (finite etale followed by an open immersion), separated (finite morphisms and immersions are separated) and of finite type, and $X$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated (Noetherian). By [thm-pqf-zmt-factorization] it factors as $V\xrightarrow{j_0}T\xrightarrow{p}X$ with $j_0$ a quasi-compact open immersion and $p$ finite. Let $Y\subseteq T$ be the closure of $j_0(V)$ with its reduced induced structure; $Y$ is closed in $T$, so $\bar f=p|_Y:Y\to X$ is finite, and $Y$ is a separated finite-type $k$-scheme of dimension $\le\dim X\le1$ (finite morphisms are integral, so they do not raise dimension). $V$ is reduced (etale over the reduced $U$), so $j_0$ factors through an open immersion $j':V\hookrightarrow Y$ with dense image, and $\bar f\circ j'=j\circ v$. The square with sides $j',v,\bar f,j$ is cartesian: $j'(V)\subseteq\bar f^{-1}(U)$ is open; the $U$-morphism $V\to\bar f^{-1}(U)$ goes from a finite $U$-scheme to a separated $U$-scheme, so it is finite, in particular closed; its image is open, closed and dense in $\bar f^{-1}(U)$, hence all of it, and as both are reduced open subschemes of $Y$ with the same underlying set, $V=U\times_XY$.

proof.text: Exchange of $j_!$ and finite direct image (Stacks Lemma 0GJ1, as used in 03SD). For the cartesian square of step 6 (open immersions $j'$, $j$; $\bar f$ finite; $v$ its base change), [lemma-weil-pbc-finite-pushforward-extension-zero] says that the comparison morphism $\beta:j_!v_*E\to\bar f_*j'_!E$ of [def-weil-pbc-finite-open-comparison] is an isomorphism for every abelian sheaf $E$ on $V_{\Et}$. With $E=v^{-1}G$ this gives $j_!v_*v^{-1}G\cong\bar f_*j'_!v^{-1}G$. By [lem-weil-pbc-curve-assertions-finite-pushforward] for the finite $\bar f:Y\to X$, it suffices to prove $\mathcal C(Y,j'_!v^{-1}G)$.

proof.text: Filtration and reduction to the constant sheaf (Stacks Lemma 03SD, end). Let $0=E_0\subset E_1\subset\cdots\subset E_m=v^{-1}G$ be the filtration of step 5, with $E_i/E_{i-1}\cong\underline{\mathbf Z/\ell}_V$. Since $j'_!$ is exact [def-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero], $0=j'_!E_0\subset\cdots\subset j'_!E_m=j'_!v^{-1}G$ is a filtration with quotients $j'_!\underline{\mathbf Z/\ell}$, i.e. there are short exact sequences $0\to j'_!E_{i-1}\to j'_!E_i\to j'_!\underline{\mathbf Z/\ell}\to0$. Step 4, applied to the reduced curve $Y$ and the open immersion $j'$, gives $\mathcal C(Y,j'_!\underline{\mathbf Z/\ell})$, and induction on $i$ with [lemma-weil-pbc-eight-curve-devissage] gives $\mathcal C(Y,j'_!E_i)$ for all $i$, in particular $\mathcal C(Y,j'_!v^{-1}G)$. By steps 7 and 5, $\mathcal C(X,j_!G)$ holds.

source.place: Section 03SB, proof of Lemma 03SD, last paragraph; Lemma 0A5C (lemma-ses-statements)

proof.text: Constructible $\mathbf F_\ell$-coefficients on a reduced curve (Stacks Theorem 03SC, proof, third and fourth paragraphs). Let $X$ be a reduced separated finite-type $k$-scheme with $\dim X\le1$, $\ell$ a prime and $G$ a constructible sheaf of $\mathbf F_\ell$-vector spaces on $X_{\Et}$. By [lem-weil-pbc-curve-dense-open-localization] there is a dense open $U=\coprod_aU_a\subseteq X$, a finite disjoint union of irreducible open subschemes $j_a:U_a\hookrightarrow X$, on which $G$ is finite locally constant, such that $\mathcal C(X,G)$ holds if and only if $\mathcal C(X,j_{a,!}(G|_{U_a}))$ holds for every $a$. Each $G|_{U_a}$ is a finite locally constant sheaf of $\mathbf F_\ell$-vector spaces on the irreducible $U_a$, so steps 5 to 8 give $\mathcal C(X,j_{a,!}(G|_{U_a}))$. Hence $\mathcal C(X,G)$ holds; in particular, when $X$ is proper over $k$, its seventh conjunct $\mathcal C_7(X,G)$ [def-weil-pbc-eight-curve-assertions] holds.

source.place: Section 03SB, proof of Theorem 03SC (theorem-vanishing-affine-curves), third and fourth paragraphs

proof.text: Reduction to reduced curves and constructible $\mathbf F_r$-coefficients, and conclusion (Stacks Theorem 03SC, proof, first two paragraphs: replace $X$ by $X_{red}$ by topological invariance 03SI, write $F$ as a filtered colimit of constructible sheaves 03SA, cohomology commutes with filtered colimits 03Q5 and pullback commutes with colimits, split off primary parts and devisse along $0\to F[\ell]\to F\to F/F[\ell]\to0$ by 0A5C). These reductions for assertion (7) are [lem-weil-pbc-curve-constructible-reduction]: for the proper curve $C$ and the torsion sheaf $F$, $\mathcal C_7(C,F)$ follows from the instances $\mathcal C_7(X,G)$ for reduced proper curves $X$ over $k$, primes $r$ and constructible $\mathbf F_r$-sheaves $G$. Those instances hold by step 9. Hence $\mathcal C_7(C,F)$ holds for every algebraically closed extension $k'/k$, which by step 1 is the statement: $\pi^*:H^q(C_{\Et},F)\to H^q((C_{k'})_{\Et},\pi^{-1}F)$ is an isomorphism for every $q\ge0$. (Bridge, added by the lead 2026-10-09: step 9 delivers constructibility in the curve sense of [def-weil-pbc-constructible-torsion]; [lem-weil-pbc-curve-constructible-reduction] asks for constructible sheaves of $\mathbf F_r$-modules in the sense of [def-weil-pbc-etale-constructible-sheaf]; the two notions agree for sheaves killed by $r$ by [lem-weil-pbc-constructible-torsion-modules-agree], applied on the reduced proper curves $X$ of step 9 with $n=r$.)
